newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Displaced pour into Angolan provincial capital.
newsitem.headline: Displaced pour into Angolan provincial capital.

text.p: Some 500 people who say they are fleeing troop movements have arrived in a provincial capital in northeast Angola, a World Food Program (WFP) official said on Wednesday.

"Our office in Saurimo says these people say they are coming into the city because of a large-scale movement of armed troops in the area," the official told Reuters, referring to the capital of Lunda Norte Province.
He said the displaced people did not say if the troops were former UNITA rebels or government soldiers.
Saurimo is about 200 km (125 miles) southwest of the area where government troops and UNITA rebels fought each other in May and June this year.

Military analysts said this government offensive into the diamond-rich UNITA-held areas in the northeast was the largest military operation since the government and UNITA signed a peace accord in 1994.

The WFP official said most of the displaced people interviewed said they had left an area around the UNITA-held town of Chiluage on the border with the Democratic Republic of the Congo, some 130 km (80 miles) east of Saurimo.
The official said nearly 175 families had arrived in Saurimo, most of them women and children. Most of the people were being taken care of by family members already in Saurimo.
